scope: Substantive refresh of an existing post at its URL, adding sources

observations.summary: All water leaves the house through one main drainage pipe into the tank; solids settle as sludge, oil and grease float as scum; compartments and a T-shaped outlet keep sludge and scum in the tank; effluent goes to the drainfield where soil treats it; an overloaded drainfield can flood, causing sewage to flow to the surface or back up into toilets and sinks.
observations.inference_limit: Federal homeowner guidance; the symptom table in the post is an interpretation labeled as starting points, not EPA text.

observations.summary: Pump if the bottom of the scum layer is within six inches of the outlet, the top of the sludge within 12 inches, or sludge and scum exceed 25 percent of liquid depth; mechanical systems generally inspected once a year.

A tank never pumped without problems may mean minimal use, a leaking tank, or a tank full of solids slowly migrating that may clog the drainfield; additives are not necessary and may decrease drainfield performance; many pumps and controls need replacement every 10 to 20 years; drainfields over 25 to 30 years old can develop a thickened biomat causing ponding, surfacing or backups.
observations.inference_limit: Federal homeowner guidance; page also lists dollar figures not repeated per site pricing policy.

observations.summary: After flooding the scum layer may lift and partially plug the outlet tee; if the system backs up into the house, check the tank first for outlet blockage.
observations.inference_limit: Reused from the flood safety refresh collected the same day.
